judgments.forked_readings_summary:
All four share a strong common envelope: add a fail-open/advisory notification capability, NO new blocking gate, NO external delivery (Slack/email/webhooks/SMS all explicitly out), and it is framework-source work (not a consumer app). Within that envelope they split into two distinct tasks on TRIGGER + MECHANISM + CONTENT.

Camp A (Readings 1 and 3): Add ONE new hooks/notify script registered under a Claude Code Notification event in hooks.json (+ run-hook.cmd shim + a behavioral test). It re-surfaces conditions preflight ALREADY computes — registration rot, dead-gate/heartbeat liveness, config/stack drift — reusing the SessionStart additionalContext warning pattern (REG_WARN/HB_WARN). Emits only when a condition is present, silent when clean. Adds NO config schema. R1 and R3 are essentially the same task (R1 enumerates lib/heartbeat.sh reuse more precisely; R3 is slightly more generic about which alerts), so A is internally near-full-agreement.

Camp B (Readings 2 and 4): The trigger is a GATE BLOCKING (exit 2) — and for R4 also a Stop/review-loop-completion. R2 is the sharpest fork: it EXPLICITLY excludes adding a new Notification hookEventName, and instead instruments the six existing exit-2 gates (pre-push-gate-check, bootstrap-write-gate, coupled-edit-gate, adjudication-output-gate, behavioral-contract-gate, rubric-validity-gate) to emit a structured 'what was blocked / why / what clears it' message via a new lib/notify.sh helper, plus re-surface unacknowledged blocks at next SessionStart, and adds a defaults/config-template.json notify block. R4 uses the new Notification-event-hook MECHANISM (like Camp A) but ties the triggering content to gate-blocks/review-loop-stops (like R2), and adds an optional config toggle + a FRAMEWORK.md honesty label, plus a Stop-event block — Stop is unique to R4.

Concrete disagreements: (1) trigger — integrity conditions at notification time (A) vs a gate blocking / loop stopping (B); (2) mechanism — one new dedicated hook (R1/R3/R4) vs modifying every existing gate + a shared helper (R2); (3) file set — add ~1 hook file (A, R4) vs edit ~6 gates + add lib helper (R2); (4) config schema — none (R1/R3) vs an opt-in notify block/toggle (R2/R4); (5) Stop event — only R4. These are different builds, not different wordings of the same build, hence a material fork held below total divergence only by the shared no-external/no-new-gate/fail-open constraints.

All four agree on the OUTER boundary (a passive/fail-open, advisory notification layer; NO external transport like Slack/email/webhook/desktop-toast; NO new blocking gate; NO change to gate exit codes; not consumer-app runtime). But the CORE — what fires the notification and what it reports — materially forks into two camps. Camp A (Readings 1 and 3): a new Notification-event hook that RE-SURFACES already-detected framework-INTEGRITY warnings (registration rot, dead-gate/stale heartbeats, config/stack drift) that would otherwise be buried in SessionStart additionalContext; adds no new detection. Camp B (Readings 2 and 4): the notification fires on a GATE BLOCK (exit 2) and/or a REVIEW-LOOP stop/complete event — reporting 'what was blocked / loop finished,' a different trigger and different information content. MECHANISM also forks, cutting across the camps: Readings 1, 3, 4 add a NEW hook script (hooks/notify) under a NEW harness event registration in hooks.json (Reading 4 uniquely also adds a Stop event), whereas Reading 2 EXPLICITLY rejects a new Notification hookEventName and instead modifies the existing exit-2 gates to emit a message on block plus a new lib/notify.sh helper and SessionStart re-surfacing. SURFACE sets diverge accordingly: 1/3/4 center on hooks/notify + hooks.json Notification block + run-hook.cmd + behavioral test; 2 centers on the 6 existing gates + session-start + lib/notify.sh. Secondary minor splits: 2 and 4 add an opt-in 'notify' config block to config-template.json while 1 and 3 explicitly exclude config-schema changes for the first cut; doc/honesty-label and installer-touch handling vary minorly. Grep confirms no existing Notification/notify surface in the framework, so all are proposing net-new work. Net: a genuine material fork on core behavior and surfaces, bounded by strong agreement on what is out of scope.

All four agree on a shared envelope: add a NET-NEW, fail-open/advisory notification surface to the framework source, never changing any gate's block/allow decision, never adding external delivery (Slack/email/webhook/desktop toast), and (where applicable) wiring a behavioral test into run-all-tests.sh and dispatching through run-hook.cmd. The scope boundary "passive, advisory, not a gate, not external transport" is essentially unanimous (minor-variation only). But the readings FORK on the two load-bearing questions — what triggers the notification and which surfaces get edited:

(A) Readings 1 and 3 — INTEGRITY-CONDITION re-surfacing via a new Claude Code `Notification`-event hook. The trigger is "a framework-integrity condition already detected elsewhere is present" (registration rot, dead-gate/stale heartbeat, config/stack drift). It adds NO new detection logic, reuses session-start/drift-detector/heartbeat output, edits only hooks/notify + hooks.json (+ test + shim), and explicitly EXCLUDES gate-script edits and any config schema.

(B) Reading 2 — GATE-BLOCK message emission, and notably it EXCLUDES adding a Claude Code `Notification` hook event entirely. Instead the trigger is "a gate decided to exit 2," and the in-scope surfaces are the six exit-2 gate scripts themselves (they emit a structured 'what/which gate/why/what clears it' message), plus a new lib/notify.sh helper sourced by those gates, plus an opt-in 'notify' block in defaults/config-template.json, plus re-surfacing unacknowledged blocks at SessionStart. This edits gate logic and adds config schema — both of which 1/3 explicitly put out of scope — and deliberately does NOT register a new hook event.

(C) Reading 4 — STRADDLES: like 1/3 it registers new harness hook events (Notification AND Stop) rather than editing gate scripts, but like 2's intent its trigger is 'a gate blocked a push or a review loop stopped/completed.' It also adds an optional config toggle and a FRAMEWORK.md honesty label.

Net: trigger semantics split integrity-conditions (1,3) vs gate-block/review-stop (2,4); mechanism splits new-Notification-hook (1,3,4) vs gates-emit-on-exit-2 with NO new hook event (2); and config schema splits out (1,3) vs in (2,4). Reading 2 would produce a diff touching different files (gate scripts, config) than 1/3 (a standalone notify hook), so behavior and surfaces materially fork even though the high-level intent (surface something to a human, passively) rhymes. The installer-edit question is only a minor variance — the installer auto-discovers hooks/ via git ls-tree and jq-merges the whole .hooks block, so 1/3 correctly call installer/verifier edits unnecessary while 2/4's framing is compatible.
